title: Unsolicited advice for AI game dev: screen feel noisy in game? Completely gut and rethink your UI and HUD
author: JeeCharns
selftext:
I’ve seen so many AI made games on here that look great, but have really busy text heavy HUD with lots of bars, lots of icons and lots of text.

You DO NOT need complex UI even if you are making a complex game.

I’m a web designer for my day job and I use AI for that too and it has the same problem. It is so trigger happy with text, UI, extra buttons, headers, CTAs.

It really kills the usability of a game and alienates people.

My unsolicited advice is to cut it all out and try to think through your HUD from first principles:  
\- imagine trying to make your HUD with no text. How would you communicate visually what things are? This is always better than text labels. Hovering can show text labels if you need them  
\- show things in game in context. Communicate in the world if you can. Lots of great games do this. Instead of showing people where to go with a big arrow, make the place they need to go well lit with a spotlight  
\- progressive disclosure: this is the most important phrase in my job for reducing clutter and cognitive load. Instead of showing every action you can do in a bar, have a button called ‘actions’, which when you click it shows you more options. 

The goal should be that the HUD is pleasant, intuitive, not overwhelming.

comments.author: Any-Gap-933
comments.body:
Time. You have to spend HOURS WEEKS to get the UI good. Make sure its consistent. Games are all about polish and not the first thing AI spits out. Example for the game I'm working on:

https://i.redd.it/8pxw5s7x8hyh1.png

replies.author: MrNotmark
replies.body: Yeah so for example these already feel noisy ro me, why are the control keys in the UI, I would say that's a waste of space

replies.author: Any-Gap-933
replies.body: Sure, you need to balance controls that a player wouldn't know until they learn them and then hide them after its muscle memory.

replies.author: MrNotmark
replies.body: Seems like a bad place to put it if you plan to hide it, put it in the corner or at the edge

replies.author: JeeCharns
replies.body: Is this for a tutorial or the HUD for all game?

replies.author: Any-Gap-933
replies.body: I'm still working on it and considering a few ideas, one being to show them initially and then hide or do what some games do where they are shown when pressing ALT or some other key and then make the UI minimal normally.

replies.author: JeeCharns
replies.body: I would have a tutorial where controls are explained once and then used in game. Once they use controls in game to do something then the muscle memory gets set and you won’t need to explain it again (but always good to have it somewhere like controls in settings)

replies.author: JeeCharns
replies.body:
I will reiterate my advice from first principles: imagine making this game with no text in the HUD. What would that look like?  
What if the controls / hotkeys were disclosed progressively so you see them once and know where to find them if you need a reminder?  
What if hull and shield damage could be shown on the hull and the shield? Then you wouldn’t need to spell out the words hull and shield. Or use icons!  
What if you didn’t have ‘align to navar’ written in 3 places in the HUD and just relied on the in game direction?  
By doing all of this you are immersing the player in the world and not taking them out of it

I would like to see the same screenshot but with nothing on screen other than the spaceship, the in game indicator of where to go to, the dialogue, and maybe the radar

replies.author: Any-Gap-933
replies.body: Love the feedback, my UI is no where near ready, I was mainly making a point that it doesn't look AI, definitely needs a ton more polish before its ready.

replies.author: JeeCharns
replies.body: Yeah it looks great! Love the sci fi aesthetic. The ship, space and sun look amazing! ❤️

comments.author: duskaception
comments.body: I like physical HUD, similar to deadspace. I made my health/mana/stam a bracelet and the UI a book you pull out. the map is a hologram spell that comes out of the book, waypoint system is similar to skyrim with clairvoyance spell.

comments.author: thecrownforge
comments.body: the no text test is useful, but i'd also try it on a small phone screen where hover doesn't exist. if players can't tell what a button does on first tap, a short label may be better than another icon

comments.author: Working-Spray-2933
comments.body: We should be building games for vr//ar imo

comments.author: Bosn1an
comments.body: Try making UI and HUD with [Envy UI](http://envyui.com) it will be automatically better without AI slop look.

comments.author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
comments.body: There's so many games that get posted here and the first thing you're in is like so many options and text. Like what happened to the start button?
